content.text:
**Choose Sentry**, unless your product is mostly mobile apps (then consider Bugsnag).

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Best at** | Broadest coverage: errors, tracing/performance, session replay, profiling | Fast, focused error grouping and alerting | Mobile and release stability tracking |
| **SDK coverage** | Largest (100+ platforms) | Good for web and backend | Strong on mobile (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter) and web |
| **Pricing model** | Per plan, with usage quotas (errors, spans, replays). Unlimited users on paid tiers | Per event volume. Unlimited users | Per seat and event volume, under SmartBear |
| **Rough cost for 10 people** | Team plan starts around $26–30/mo, higher with overages | Low entry price, rising with event volume | Typically the priciest of the three at this size |
| **Self-hosting** | Yes (source-available) | No | No |
| **Ecosystem** | Largest community, many integrations (GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear) | Solid integrations | Solid integrations, plus the SmartBear suite |
| **Weaknesses** | Quota and overage tuning needed. The UI has a lot of features | Fewer features beyond errors. Smaller community | Narrower feature set. Cost scales with seats |

**Why Sentry for a 10-person team**
- **No per-seat pricing.** Adding teammates doesn't raise the bill.
- **Room to grow.** If you later want tracing or session replay, you won't need another vendor.
- **Largest SDK coverage and community.** Setup is easy and answers are easy to find.
- **Self-hosting is an exit option** if cost or data residency becomes a concern.

**When to pick something else**
- **Bugsnag:** you ship mainly mobile apps and want its release health and stability score as the main metric.
- **Rollbar:** you only want error tracking, with simple pricing and minimal setup, and don't need the other Sentry features.

My pricing figures come from memory and these vendors change plans often. Check current pricing pages before committing. All three have free tiers, so you can run a one- or two-week trial on a real service. Compare how well each groups errors and how noisy the alerts are, since those matter more than features in daily use.

If you tell me your stack and monthly error volume, I can estimate costs more precisely.
